articleTitle: Challenges in Offshore Power Systems: Pushing HVAC Transmission to the Limit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: During the early design stage, it was decided to use High Voltage Alternating Current (HVAC) power transmission to provide power to a large offshore field. Long 230 kV rated submarine cables were utilized to transfer AC power to wellhead platforms with Electrical Submersible Pumps (ESPs) required for artificial lifting. Shunt Reactors are used for voltage control and to maximize power transfer capability through submarine cables. This combination poses various challenges in steady state operation and switching transients. This paper discusses some of the challenging aspects of such application, including shunt reactor sizing, transient recovery voltage and voltage transformer (VT) discharge. In addition, this paper presents various simulations performed to select optimal system parameters and configurations for successful system operation. Reactive compensation configuration and control will be discussed along with the potential delayed zero crossing phenomena.

articleTitle: Predictive Motor Failure Prevention in Refinery Using Cloud Based Motor Current Signature Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: As the industrial world is evolving into Industry 4.0, connected products allow for greater visualization and awareness of the status of critical assets. The collection, analysis, and communication of data from these assets allow insight into the status of equipment, along with the level of wear and lifespan of this equipment. Diagnosing the current health of each asset gives stakeholders advanced warning to possible failures, which pose significant safety and financial risks. Internet of things (IOT) connected products allow for real-time monitoring and have the benefit of data processing in the cloud where historical data can be easily used to analyze potential failures. For over the last 10 years, vibration analysis paired with artificial intelligence has become a common method for motor failure identification. Motor Current Signature Analysis (MCSA) is a novel, non-invasive method that leverages recently available cloud processing power to deliver very similar predictive results comparable to vibration analysis. For critical motors, MCSA allows for a non-invasive, easy to install, and cost-effective motor monitoring method. In this paper, we will explore two main topics: 1) The MCSA data journey for critical motors where details are being continuously collected and transferred to a cloud-based analytics platform where they are compared on a data lake with other similar motors across the world to improve prediction and failure detection algorithms over time. 2) The detection and analysis of three different motor failure modes using Motor Current Signature Analysis on low voltage motors at a Refinery.

articleTitle: Experience With On-Line Ground Fault Protection in Medium Voltage Drive Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The uniqueness of medium voltage AC drive systems requires attention to ground fault protection. Most often these power conversion topologies include an isolation rectifier transformer with multiple secondaries, a converter-inverter, and the motor stator windings. The internal ground fault protection of the adjustable frequency drive can be configured for continuity of operation or immediate shutdown to ensure personnel safety and minimize equipment damage. Ground fault protection included within the AFD electronics can be configured for programmable voltage pick up thresholds. This paper will introduce the many topologies of MV AFDs and then presents protection results from multiple locations from a high-impedance to frame ground system.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Model To Simulate Vertical Motors and Calculate Reed Critical Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper provides a mathematical model for calculating the reed critical frequency (RCF) of vertical motors on a massive rigid base. Typical methods of predicting RCF of vertical motors are performing a bump test on the motor or performing a full model simulation using Finite Element Analysis (FEA) or following the method given by NEMA where a motor could be considered as a single degree of freedom spring-mass system and static deflection at its center of gravity. However, these methods can sometimes prove to be expensive as well as time consuming. Another challenge is to predict RCF accurately so as to avoid any chance of harmonic interaction with driven equipment. This makes it crucial for motor manufacturers to submit motor outlines with RCF within +/−10% accuracy. The discussed model in this paper considers a vertical motor as a two degree of freedom spring-mass system and calculates RCF after simplifying the complete motor into equivalent structures using beam theory. This mathematical model is developed for calculating static deflection, the center of gravity and RCF for vertical motors where a user could select different enclosures, configurations and predict RCF. This model not only optimizes resources but provides accurate RCF.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Standards, Practices, Guides, Specifications, and Codes & Regulations: How to Maximize Their Benefit in the Petrochemical Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The design, fabrication, purchasing, installation, testing, maintenance, and retirement of electrical systems and equipment found in petrochemical facilities are defined in various types of documents. These documents can be in the form of Standards, Practices, Guides, Specifications, and Codes & Regulations. This paper discusses the differences between these document types, how these documents are developed, when each of the documents should be used, and how to maximize their benefits when used within the petrochemical industry.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of SVPD-PWM and Multiband Hysteresis Through Digital Implementation for A Type-G Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: In last decades, aiming to control some processes and improve high power systems efficiency, multilevel converters have commonly been used in adjustable speed and high-performance drives in the mining industry. Although they present operational advantages over the classic two-level topology in high power and medium voltage applications, current control employed for them has yet some issues that deserve additional studies. In this line, this work presents a comparative study of two current control techniques for a five-level Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) induction motor drive: (i) linear current control with SVPWM command (commonly applied in commercial drives) and (ii) non-linear digital hysteresis current control. A multiband switching frequency limiter is proposed in this paper for the last technique. The multilevel power electronic converter investigated here is an NPC converter known as Type G converter. Some challenges for implementation of digital multiband hysteresis are discussed. In this paper a digital signal processor (DSP) is proposed for both strategies, while a field programmable gate array (FPGA) is employed to implement the frequency limiting circuits and switching logic of the digital hysteresis control. In both cases, the drive operates under rotor field-oriented control (RFOC). Results obtained from Simulation in PLECS™ are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Modern Ied Data Capture Configuration Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Modern digital protective devices, sometimes called Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs), typically have a vast array of data collecting capabilities, but a finite memory in which to store the collected data. Errors in IED configuration can result in critical data being missing or obscured, either because it wasn’t captured or because the available memory was full of irrelevant data. For example, many IEDs can store information concerning protective function type, pick-up value, timestamp, and power system values immediately before, during and following a trip event. Almost every parameter or variable and a wide variety of analog data can be stored. When configured appropriately, this data can simplify fault investigations, expedite power system restoration and provide valuable data for avoiding future incidents. Hence, there is great value in understanding the digital protective relay, the application, and the common failure modes at the outset when configuring a digital protective relay. The purpose of this paper is to recommend IED data storage schemes for commonly encountered applications based on the collective experiences of the authors.

articleTitle: Development of a Novel Method For Continuous Neutral Grounding Resistor Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Neutral resistance grounding has been utilized to make power systems safer for more than 70 years. There are conditions where a resistively grounded power system can become unsafe, and those instances can be discovered through continuous monitoring of the NGR resistance value and parasitic loss impedance. Upon measuring a hazardous condition, the power system can be de-energized. Continuous monitoring devices have been developed and deployed but have shortcomings when measuring the value of the neutral grounding resistor and non-fundamental frequency ground-fault currents. The authors describe a novel monitoring system to accurately measure the resistance value of the neutral grounding resistor (NGR), the impedance of parasitic losses between the neutralizing point and protective-earth, evaluate non-fundamental frequency ground-fault current, and reduce nuisance tripping. The elements of the proposed device are discussed and analyzed in detail. Results from testing components of the proposed method are provided and discussed.

articleTitle: Improving Electrical Safety: The Next Level
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Despite numerous efforts to increase safety during electrical work activities, we regularly receive notifications or read in newspapers about incidents with electricity resulting in severe injuries or even fatalities. Many of these incidents are related to attitude or moments of carelessness. Can we do something about it? A joint effort of employers, the electrical worker and their colleagues could provide an incentive to influence attitude and change behaviors by all stakeholders and create a culture that embraces values that do not accept deviations from the norm. This paper describes various ways in which an electrical safety culture can be established or improved.

articleTitle: Management of Electric Motors Lifecycle At Oil & GAS Industrial Facilities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper presents the experience and lessons learned in the development and implementation of a motors condition assessment methodology at a large oil & gas company. Having a huge fleet of new and aging assets, the management of these assets becomes ever more critical. Accordingly, to ensure operational reliability and continuity, and to assure the continued cost-effectiveness of existing assets, a methodology had to be developed to manage the assets, extend their life, and timely plan for their replacement prior to failure.Accordingly, a criterion was developed to initially prioritize the large number of critical motors for assessment, and identify their applicability. Afterwards, the motor assessment relied on the use of existing motor operational data, complemented with offline testing data identified from international procedures and best practices. Based on the identified data results, a scoring system was established to determine the motor condition.The electric motor management program is contributing to minimizing motor failures, while deferring capital expenditures in replacements, by relying on cost-effective testing and overhauling practices as opposed to equipment failures and unplanned operational interruptions. Such practices will extend the economic life of the electrical motors, while maintaining the required operational safety and availability.

articleTitle: Auditing Your Electrical Safety Management Program. : A method to identify key gaps in electrical safety at your site.
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Auditing is a critical element of an electrical safety program. This paper explores the use of auditing as an essential element of any safety program. Auditing provides the means to understand performance versus established standards. Auditing identifies key gaps in electrical safety areas for continuous improvement. To have an effective electrical safety program, an auditing process must be an integral element of the electrical safety program. This paper discusses the incorporation, process, and benefits of auditing as a key element in an electrical safety management program.

articleTitle: Minimizing Rolling Element Bearing Failures in Electric Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: In recent years bearing failures have accounted for an increased percentage of motor failures. This may be due in part to improved stator and rotor construction coupled with higher efficiency and lower heating losses. Bearings are often acknowledged to be the “weak link” of rotating equipment if not properly maintained. According to the Electrical Apparatus Service Association (EASA) Bearing failures account for over half of all premature motor failures. This paper addresses ways to reduce the rate of bearing failures in electric motors.

articleTitle: Consideration of Bus Protection on Gas-Insulated Switchgear, A Three-Phase Fault Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: One design benefit of gas-insulated switchgear is its sealed bus design that reduces the chance of bus short circuit fault. Since the costs of implementing a bus protection scheme can be significant, engineers sometimes forgo designing a bus protection scheme for gas-insulated switchgear due to its robust design. This paper reviews a special case of a three-phase fault on the bus of a 34.5 kV gas-insulated switchgear that did not have a dedicated bus protection scheme. The sequence of events, impact, and root causes are outlined as a case study. From the findings revealed in the incident, bus protection was re-evaluated for installation on the existing gas-insulated switchgear. Retrofit options are presented and compared to each other in terms of effectiveness, complexity, and cost.

articleTitle: Load Commutated Inverter Modeling: Impacts and Solutions for an Isolated Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper explores the impact of several medium-voltage load commutated inverter motor drives on an industrial power system. The impacts of load commutated inverter transients on the facility’s power system, the external utility grid, and its remedial protection and control systems are explored through modeling the load commutated drive system, protection devices, and the control system with a real-time control hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

articleTitle: The Integral Role of Electric Motors in Achieving Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Globally, electric motors are the single biggest converters of electrical energy, accounting for an estimated 45 % of the world’s electricity usage. Even as the world transitions to more sustainable energy sources, global electricity consumption is anticipated to increase. Improving the efficiency of electric motors is an integral part of reducing the total energy usage, though it only makes up one portion of a motor’s total sustainability footprint. From the sourcing of raw materials used to manufacture a motor and their circularity to the greenhouse gases emitted during the transportation of the motor to its final installation site, this paper provides a holistic view of sustainability regarding electric motors and guidance for assuring sustainability in motor selection.

articleTitle: Design for Reliability (DFR) of DC-Link Capacitors for Multilevel Inverter Topologies Operating in Hostile Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Especially in the mining industry, Pulse Width Modulated Voltage Source Converters (PWM-VSC) driving induction motors at long distances from the inverter is common. Due to the long cable used for the converter-to-motor connection, several unwanted high-frequency phenomena occur. A new configuration for these motor drive systems was previously proposed to address this situation. The new configuration involves keeping the rectifier in its original location, while the inverter bridge is installed close to the motor terminals, and long cables are used as a DC transmission line. The environment in which the inverter will now be located is more hostile and can compromise the inverter’s lifetime. This situation creates new concerns about the system’s reliability, despite the various advantages of this new configuration. This paper presents a study on the reliability of the DC-Link capacitors for Three Level Neutral Point Clamped (3L-NPC) and Three Level Active Neutral Point Clamped (3L-ANPC) inverter topologies when operating in aggressive environments. For this purpose, methodologies based on Physics of Failure (PoF) and Design for Reliability (DfR) were used. In this sense, an investigation was conducted to find the configurations best suited to improve the solution regarding reliability, cost, energy, and volume.

articleTitle: Safety Through Speed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper expands on the relationship between fault interrupting speed versus incident energy. It will provide some details about the world’s fastest low voltage (LV) circuit breaking technology. With ultra-fast and consistent clearing times, devices using this technology provide the fastest method of removing fault currents. This sequentially reduces fault incident energies to nearly non-existent levels. Adding this switching technology could be the next step in enhancing your safety program. This new and very rapidly growing technology is the LV Solid-State Circuit Breaker (SSCB). Using silicon carbide (SiC) semiconductor modules, and unique current sensing methodologies, furnishes the SSCB with the ability to provide extremely rapid, consistent, and arc-less switching. Since the interruption of the current is performed without any electro-mechanical contacts, these devices can provide an almost unlimited number of switching operations. While at the same time, release virtually no arc flash incident energy whilst also limiting the let-through current to the lowest level in industry. In this work we will provide an overview of this newtechnology and how Petroleum and Chemical industry users can take advantage of eliminating almost all release of arc flash incident energy associated with traditional LV molded case circuit breakers (MCCB). And, at the same time, significantly reduce the electromechanical stress on the connected load and virtually eliminating the need for breaker maintenance!

articleTitle: Considerations for Making the Switch from Steam Turbines to Large Motor Drives for Ethylene Plants
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: In many locations, due to a motivation for decarbonization, emission reductions and the need for replacement of aging equipment, electric motors are being considered as replacements for steam turbine drives on the primary ethylene plant compressors. This paper will explore the considerations in switching from a steam turbine drive in terms of electric motor controls, motor starts / stops, variable frequency drive (VFD) sizing for motor starting, speed / torque curves and the possibility of compressor modifications (speed changes, rewheels<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, or rotor change-outs for higher efficiencies). This project relies on previous experiences as a supplier with large power (>20 MW) motor drive replacement projects worldwide at various ethylene / propylene refinery sites.

Author Keywords: Adjustable speed drive (ASD) or VFD / VSD

articleTitle: Cable Sizing Flowchart - A Tool To Help Reinforce The State of Electrical Engineering Workforce
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: In the last decade, maybe longer, the oil, gas and chemical (OGC) industry has seen a decline in the electric power engineering ranks and knowledge base. With the advent of the pandemic and the great resignation that followed, the industry has seen an acceleration of this knowledge drain. As experienced workers retire, knowledge around engineering and design of electrical systems and the application of various products is leaving with them, and hence engineers are being tasked with doing more sooner. Many universities have shifted the focus of their curriculums to cater to the field of high tech, leaving only a handful of institutions with strong programs in electric power engineering and subfields such as electric machines, power electronics, and power systems. Addressing skill gaps has become a point of discussion from break rooms to board rooms. One clear example is the sizing of Medium and Low Voltage power cables, that are critical to the supply of electric power in all industries. Selecting and sizing cables can have a material impact on the overall reliability, safety, and the CAPEX cost of a project.This paper discusses the state of engineers retiring and resigning in the industry causing knowledge and training gaps and give examples of a cable selection tool. The tool brings relevant knowledge that resides in IEEE, and the National Electrical Code (NEC) around cables and selecting the right size of cable using Low Voltage Cable Sizing Flowchart in appendix A, based on 2023 NEC. The goals of the paper are to expose the knowledge and training crisis to a widespread audience and then to provide a handy reference cable sizing guide for the early career professional who is asked to make cable selection, and to serve as a springboard for further reference depending on the specific application that the engineer might be tasked with.

articleTitle: Evolution of Very High Power (>15 MW) Medium Voltage Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Very high power adjustable speed motor applications above 15 MW historically used Load Commutated Inverter drives coupled to designed for purpose synchronous motors. These systems required detailed application engineering for the particular site to mitigate potential power factor, line harmonics, torque pulsation, and motor design requirements. In the past decade manufacturers have started offering Voltage Source Inverter PWM drives at these power levels, up to 13.8 kV motor voltage for both induction and synchronous motors, which have fewer application complications. These large drives were initially based on either 5-level Neutral Point Clamped or Cascaded H Bridge topologies, usually limited to 11 kV, but now some manufacturers are utilizing Modular Multilevel Converters for the very high power, applications with voltages above 11 kV. The Modular Multilevel Converter topology will be further explored together with its application to these medium voltage motors.

articleTitle: Reduced Rated Adjustable Speed Drives Starting for High Power Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: There is a large installed base of very large motors above 10 MW that have been started with across the line starters or breakers rated 6.9 kV to 13.8 kV. With changes in the power utility networks and more stringent voltage drop allowances, they may no longer be allowed to start across the line, but starting torque requirements could prevent reduced voltage starting. One option is to utilize reduce rated adjustable speed drives for either induction or synchronous motors to bring the motor up to speed. This paper will describe how to size an adjustable speed drive for starting duty applications. The same sizing requirements can be applied for new applications as well as complete retrofits of an older engines and turbines with an electric motor.

articleTitle: Modernizing a Refinery Brushless Motor P&C System to Maximize Availability – a Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper presents a case study of a retrofit project that updated the excitation control system and motor protection on several brushless, synchronous motors at a major refinery in Texas, USA. Due to aging, failing components in the original excitation control system, the facility experienced recurring unexpected motor shutdowns. This paper discusses the solution that was developed and implemented on these motors, which consisted of replacing outdated components in the exciter supply and control circuitry with simple, adjustable DC power supplies controlled by an updated protection and control relay. As a result of this retrofit, the motors continue to run ideally under automatic control, with significantly reduced system maintenance. The new design increased system reliability and decreased the likelihood of an unexpected shutdown due to an inadvertent component failure.

articleTitle: Integrating Renewable Energy Behind-The-Meter In Upstream Oil and Gas Operations - Part II
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The cost of solar photovoltaic power has decreased over the past 15 years making it an attractive option for oil and gas companies to cost-effectively reduce their Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions. This paper is the $2^{{\mathrm {nd}}}$ paper in a two-part series describing the integration of behind-the-meter solar PV in an upstream oil and gas operation, using a case study based mainly on solar power plants being installed in West Texas and New Mexico, as well as one commissioned in California in 2020. The first paper covered the feasibility, organization, early concept engineering, and project development of behind-the-meter solar power in an oil and gas operation. This paper discusses the engineering, design, commissioning, and initial operation of the solar farm. The authors explore the technical aspects specific to integrating these farms in operational oil and gas environments plus the economic and logistic challenges faced during execution.

articleTitle: High Performance Control of Power Converters in Mining Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Various modern control concepts have been developed over the last decades. Despite that, due to real-time computational constraints, standard linear controllers continue to dominate in industry applications of power converters. On the other hand, demanding applications (for example, mining excavating machines) can benefit from advanced performance offered by modern control schemes. To this aim, the current paper develops advanced control structures using principles of Optimal control, Predictive control and Kalman observers. To ensure their easy implementation with industrial variable speed drives (VSD), the paper expresses the proposed novel structures in the form similar to the standard (PI or PR) control. The paper then demonstrated the advantages of the proposed advanced control schemes by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Fundamentals of Microgrid Dead Bus Arbitration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: A microgrid is a smaller electric network that can operate independently of a main power grid. An islanded microgrid is typically energized by a generator or inverter and the closing of its associated circuit breaker into a dead bus. A synchronism check is a typical function of programmable protective relays (PPRs) that supervise the closing of these breakers. The source’s voltage and frequency must be in synchronism with the bus voltage prior to closing this breaker. However, in an islanded microgrid energization scenario, a synchronism check cannot be achieved when the bus voltage is dead. Protective relays that attempt to close into a dead bus cannot differentiate between a failed potential transformer (PT) supply and a true dead bus condition. A failed PT supply presents itself as a dead bus voltage condition to the protective relay controlling the generator or inverter breaker. This can create a potentially hazardous situation when a protective relay might close a live machine’s breaker into a live bus that is out of synchronism. This paper explains the problem associated with dead bus arbitration and the various failure modes of PT voltages that necessitate a dead bus arbitration scheme. Typical microprocessor PPR solutions for dead bus close supervision of synchronization systems are also presented. In addition, this paper discusses a scenario with an inverter-based resource (IBR) energizing a dead bus and limitations that need to be considered.

articleTitle: Ushering in a New Era of Power Management for a Centenarian Oil Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper presents a state-of-the-art power management system that was commissioned for an energy corporation at its central California oil field. This field consists of several reclosers dispersed over a wide geographic area. The electrical power requirements of the plant are met by 3 cogeneration plants, comprising 8 generators with a total installed capacity of around 25 MW and 1 utility tie-line connection. In the event of a disruptive blackout, the consequent downtime results in the loss of critical production and revenue, which necessitates a solution involving a smart and high-speed power management system. The power management system solution consists of load-shedding schemes that are contingency-based, underfrequency-based, progressive-based, and wireless radio-based. The solution also includes systems for supervisory control and data acquisition, automatic generation control, voltage control, islanding control, tie-line control, and advanced automatic synchronization. Additionally, there is a high-speed generation-shedding system that sheds excess generation to prevent generators from dropping under the environmental (NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>) emissions limit. This power management system has been commissioned successfully and has been in service since September 2019. This paper discusses different power management system capabilities, design philosophy, communications architecture, data flow, hardware-in-the-loop testing using a real-time, transient-level computer model of the power system, onsite lessons learned, field implementation, and real-time events that have occurred since the commissioning of this system.

articleTitle: Variable Shunt Reactor Control for Voltage Compensation for Submarine Cable at Offshore Facility
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a shunt reactor controller (SRC) that provides voltage stability at an offshore and onshore oilfield with a gas and oil separation plant (GOSP) having 90 km submarine cables with different cross sections. There are a total of six shunt reactors (four sets at the 230 kV onshore substation and two sets at the offshore substation). The SRC also coordinates with a utility (UT) transformer tap control to avoid hunting. In addition, the SRC avoids submarine cable overloading. The paper discusses control philosophy, stepwise methodology, energization, and de-energization sequence for various loading and unloading conditions. The paper also covers different methodologies used to finalize the SRC philosophy to develop the band control strategy and discusses the load-shedding implementation to avoid overloading on submarine cables and UT transmission lines. The SRC and load-shed control system has been tested and validated using hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation to reduce commissioning challenges.

articleTitle: Concepts for Hybrid Electric Motor-Gas Turbine Driven Compressors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The combination of electric motor and gas turbine drivers to power a centrifugal compressor offers opportunities to take advantage of the individual strengths of each drive in a single package. It also creates a few technical challenges. When we talk about hybrid drives, several architectures are feasible, and the choice depends to a large degree on the project objectives. These could include optimizing efficiency, increasing power for specific situations (high ambient temperatures, starting, upset process conditions), the capability to optimize fuel cost by taking advantage of temporary price differences between gas and electricity, or the increase of availability if one fuel source is temporarily unavailable and managing emissions. The large fluctuation in the availability of electricity from renewable sources can create interesting opportunities.The combination of gas turbines and electric drives can lead to trains where one of the drivers can be decoupled, and it can also lead to drives where electricity export is possible. The paper addresses technical challenges, such as torsional train behavior, and the management of the different power sources, and it will describe the preferred train architectures depending on the project objectives.

articleTitle: Selecting Current Transformers and Relay Settings for Low Impedance Differential Relaying
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Two common questions are raised when applying differential protection: how do I select the right class and ratio of Current Transformers (CTs)? What pickup, slope, and other settings should be used in the differential relay? Several traditional methods of selecting current transformers often fall short by recommending CTs that are impractically large to fit in the available space, or too small to reproduce the fault current waveforms. This paper demonstrates how to use waveform analysis to optimize CT selection without using CTs larger than necessary for the application. The paper also shows how waveform analysis is used to calculate and validate pickup and slope settings.

articleTitle: Alternative Technology Trends and Returns of Experience of Compression Services Driven by Variable High-Speed Induction Motors Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Over the past three decades, the introduction of high-speed induction motors has enabled the electrification of various compression services. This paper aims to provide feedback from end users and manufacturers of compression trains using direct electric drives. The first part of the article presents the technology coverage of induction motors and voltage frequency drives up to 100 MW, including the use of active magnetic bearings as a replacement for oil lubricated bearings, and replacement opportunities for gas and steam turbines. The second part reviews the existing architectures of electric compression trains in operation, commissioning, or design phases, for compressor services, covering standalone and integrated motor-compressor systems. Returns of Experience and recommendations are also presented, focusing on the reasons that led the end-user to migrate their compression services to high-speed electric, including gas monetization, reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and process flexibility, highlighting the benefits in term of CAPEX and OPEX.

articleTitle: Power Automation on a Floating Production System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: One of the most critical aspects of power generation and distribution for an offshore production facility is reliability. Safety for those onboard the vessel and the ability to deliver maximum production are dependent on the availability of electrical power. Due to its critical nature, keeping power available should not be prone to delays or human errors, and thus requires an effective Power Management System (PMS) that is automated to control electrical equipment during real-time unexpected events.Power automation should be implemented in the PMS to maximize stability and availability, as well as to avoid any mis-operations or over-operations. Examples of this automation are fast power-based load shedding, automatic transformer and tie selection, automated restoration of the power system, and automated backup power transfer schemes.It is important to recognize that critical facility operations should only be enhanced by an integrated PMS and should not be dependent on such equipment. To this point, the Power System should still include the necessary hardwired interlocks to ensure the safety of personnel. Another important point regarding personnel safety is that the PMS allows for remote switching, using the graphical interface allows for reliable and common sense switching without the need for an individual to stand in front of the energized equipment. This paper will elaborate, using a real-world project, on how a power management system can automate the electrical system of an offshore platform to keep it safe, reliable, and stable.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Fundamentals - Not Just for Industrial Control Systems When Guidance and Direction are Available
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are important to supporting US critical infrastructure and maintaining national security. ICS owners and operators continue to face threats from a variety of adversaries whose intentions include gathering intelligence, stealing intellectual property, obtaining financial compensation through ransom, and disrupting national critical infrastructures. The ICS discussed do not just include control systems but often include electrical assets (microprocessor-based relays, trip units, etc.) which have been networked together using various communication protocols. Previous IEEE PCIC papers have mentioned cybersecurity without providing details on how to secure an ICS. This paper describes the issues that ICS owners and operators face and introduces the International Society of Automation (ISA)/International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 62443 [1] –[10] series of standards as the basis for an effective cybersecurity program. These standards have been developed by the ISA99 committee of the International Society of Automation and IEC Technical Committee 65 Working Group 10.

Author Keywords: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems

articleTitle: Evaluating a New Configuration for Medium-Voltage Drive Systems in a Mining Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Large AC motors are ubiquitous in the mining industry, and these often require medium-voltage (MV) converters. Generally, long cables provide the connection between the variable speed drive (VSD) and the motor, which increases problems involving high frequency currents and overvoltages. These undesired phenomena are attenuated by large, heavy and expensive inverter output filters. As an alternative solution to such problems, the authors have proposed, in previous works, the separation of the frequency converter into its rectifier and inverter units, where the rectifier remains in its original location and the inverter is placed beside the motor, thus establishing a DC transmission link through the long cable. Such a configuration naturally (i) mitigates the high-frequency phenomena, (ii) reduces the voltage drop along the cable, and (Hi) can result in substantial copper savings. Until the present moment, the evaluations performed on the proposed topology was aimed at low voltage mining applications, which have shown excellent results. However, since MV drive systems are common in the mining industry, the proposed drive topology should also be analyzed considering this application. In this way, this paper evaluates the copper and energy savings obtained through this alternative drive topology by means of a case study involving three MV motor drive systems situated in a mining plant.

articleTitle: Online Estimation of Stator Resistance In Induction Machines Using the Zero-Sequence Component of the Stator Current
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Monitoring the energy consumption and efficiency of line-connected induction motors is an important task in industry to ensure economical operation and for condition monitoring purposes. Motor efficiency which is the application intended in this paper, is conveniently obtained from airgap torque and rotational speed. Torque is easily calculated from stator voltages and currents and depends on only one machine parameter, the stator resistance. Among the existing stator resistance estimation methods that require these variables, this work is focused on the one that uses zero-sequence components of stator voltages and currents. It is easily applicable to induction machines connected directly to the mains. Zero-sequence current circulation requires the center terminal of the machine winding be connected to the neutral terminal of the voltage source for a short period of time. This work proposes the use of the zero sequence component existing in the voltage supply as the voltage to be injected. The addition of a simple pulse generator circuit to obtain a more controllable voltage is also evaluated. Implementation issues and performance characteristics of these methods are presented and discussed. Computer simulations and experimental results were obtained on a 15 hp motor test bench and used to validate the method.

articleTitle: VFD With Evaporative Liquid Cooling for Extreme Conditions in Oil and Gas Installations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Large electric motors and variable frequency drives (VFDs), also known as adjustable speed drives (ASDs), rated 5 MW and above, are now widely used in the Oil and Gas industry for their reliability, efficiency, and operational flexibility. A proper selection of the electric motor and VFD technologies is paramount to meet the desired performance, optimize capital expenditure and guarantee reliability with the lowest possible operational cost. The offshore and onshore oil and gas industry is always targeting more efficient systems to optimize production platforms, refineries, and processes related to this industry. Use of high-power VFDs becomes attractive in this scenario, as losses decrease and the impact of transient conditions is minimized during startup of large motors or short circuit condition and speed control. VFD technologies typically require controlled ambient conditions, affecting the electric room HVAC (Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning) system. Therefore, these applications focus on electric equipment as small and efficient as possible to minimize the impact on the layout and utility systems. These opposing necessities directly relate to the efficiency of the VFD cooling system. This paper will propose possible solution based on the evaporative liquid heatsink, where the results obtained from a 5.6 MW VFD case study demonstrates better thermal performance and an optimized design for oil and gas requirements.

articleTitle: Turnaround Risk Mitigation in Electrical Capital Projects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: A key risk in refinery capital projects is executing the work during a planned turnaround (TAR). To minimize risk, requires a project approach that shifts work to a non-TAR time frame. A recent successful project conducted in a Southern California refinery, reduced the project’s TAR activities from 37 to 12 days all by defining new, additional non-TAR activities. This paper discusses the work performed, the decisions made, and the challenges faced in that project, and proposes opportunities to minimize the TAR scope in electrical substation replacement and upgrade projects.

articleTitle: Comparison of Low-Voltage Arc-Resistant Equipment, Equipment with Isolation Barriers, and Equipment with Energy-Reducing Line-Side Isolation for Reduction of Arc Flash Hazards
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Arc-resistant equipment, isolation barriers, and energy-reducing line-side isolation (ERLSI) are different solutions for arc flash hazard reduction that on the surface appear to be very similar, but when considered in detail are quite different. Arc-resistant equipment redirects or contains an internal arc fault within the equipment so that the under certain conditions personnel are exposed to a lower arc-flash hazard. An isolation barrier installed in equipment can, under the right conditions, substantially lower the likelihood of inadvertent contact across the barrier. ERLSI is an equipment feature that is similar to an isolation barrier, but with enhanced functionality and applied to the line-side of the equipment main overcurrent protective device to reduce arc-flash hazards. All three solutions, when properly applied, reduce the arc flash risk to the electrical worker but under different conditions.This paper compares the application of these three solutions based upon considerations of selection, limitations, benefits, conditions under which arc-flash hazards are reduced, maintenance, end of life, and relative cost.

articleTitle: ARC-Flash Calculations: DGUV-I 203-077 vs. IEEE 1584
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: It is globally recognized that IEEE 1584 is used to calculate the prospective incident energy for selecting arc rated clothing and personal protective equipment. The information brochure DGUV-I 203-077 describes an alternative calculation method to IEEE 1584. The DGUV-I 203077 Guide has been developed and used in Germany for the selection of Arc Rated PPE. DGUV is the German Social Accident Insurance Institution which is the national, compulsory program that insures workers for injuries or illness incurred through their employment. Used by several countries, this document continues to be promoted globally as a preferred alternative to IEEE 1584. This paper explores the history of DGUV-I 203-077, why there are two incompatible arc flash calculation methods and a detailed comparison of DGUV-I 203-077 and IEEE 1584.

articleTitle: Experience In Retrofilling of Mineral Insulating Liquid Filled Transformers With Ester Liquids
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Ester liquids have been used in transformer applications for over four decades and are known to be fire safe, environmentally friendly and they can improve the life of insulation systems when compared to mineral insulating liquid (mineral oil). These dielectric liquids are increasingly being used to retrofill (removal and replacement of one insulating liquid with another) transformers filled with mineral insulating liquid to improve the fire safety of the transformer and equipment around it, extend the life of the transformer and make the transformers environmentally friendly. This paper will discuss the differences in the dielectric liquids and the properties that affect the transformer design and the effects on the performance of the transformer after a retrofill. Details will be provided on how to determine if a transformer is a candidate for retrofill and the retrofilling process. A relevant industry case study will be examined regarding transformers that have been retrofilled and the in-service condition of the transformers.

articleTitle: Testing and Commissioning of Integrated Protection and Control Solutions for Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Synchronous motors are a backbone of industrial processes. When not properly protected and controlled, unplanned disruption of the industrial process resulting from any motor failure can lead to millions of dollars in loss of revenue. Unlike induction motors, brush-type synchronous motors not only require protection of the stator winding also require a complete protection of the DC field winding, squirrel-cage winding and stationary or rotating excitation system. The first part of this paper presents the control solution that provides functions for motor starting, field application, stabilization, auto-loading $\backslash $ unloading, auto-resynchronization and automatic regulation of the DC field winding. The second part of the paper discusses various lessons learned during testing and commissioning of the integrated solution applied on a synchronous motor (SM) running a compressor application.

articleTitle: Power Management System Challenges of Upgrading Gas Turbines From Simple Cycle to Combined Cycle for the Oilfield
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper presents the challenges to a power management system that were introduced during the upgrade of an existing oil field from a simple cycle gas turbine to a combined cycle gas turbine. The combined cycle block consists of three gas turbines and one steam turbine from two manufacturers. The paper discusses the impact to processes during the upgrade and main milestones of commissioning the steam turbine. New modes of running steam turbines that were introduced are compared with the existing gas turbines. Steam coupling between the gas turbine and steam turbine is presented that includes high-pressure and low-pressure steam calculations and associated steam turbine output power. The impacts of the steam coupling to the existing generation control system and load shedding system are explained. Steam equations of the model and the slow response impact to the electric power system model are also presented.

articleTitle: Letting The Smoke Out - What To Do If Your Motor Fails
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: In the course of experiencing a failure of a large electrical machines, it is prudent for operations to bring the equipment back into service as quickly as possible. However, from the standpoint of long-term reliability it is best to attempt to understand the failure, its cause, and corrective action to prevent recurrence. Motor failure mechanisms can be associated with four general categories: Thermal, Electrical, Ambient, and Mechanical. These categories encompass issues with loading, power systems, lubrication, contamination, and more. The aim of this paper is to provide the end user or service technician with a guide and checklist on what information or operational data to gather, which testing to perform, and generally, how to initiate the investigation of common failure mechanisms.

articleTitle: Alternative Methods of Machine Online Condition Monitoring; Recommendations for Rotating Machines in Petroleum and Chemical Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Rotating machines health assessment is an important aspect of machine operation. There are several online tests and techniques available to assess machine condition during service. Online condition monitoring and assessment helps to detect changes in machine operating condition at an early stage as well as determining the degree of degradation over time. Assessing machine condition can help estimate the risk of failure and the potential vulnerability to unexpected or unintended operating events. The objective is to promptly initiate corrective measures preventing costly shutdowns and production losses. The online monitoring is also helpful in being well prepared ahead of scheduled shutdown. In this paper, individual online tests and monitoring techniques are discussed on both synchronous and induction machines rated between 4.0 kV and up to 13.8 kV. The online monitoring techniques covered are; rotor flux monitoring, stator endwinding vibration monitoring, broken rotor bar detection, stator inter-turn fault detection and online partial discharge monitoring. A systematic approach based on years of experience and field studies is presented to provide a clear path for selecting appropriate tests and to choose an optimized and best possible online monitoring techniques that can be used in the Petroleum and Chemical Industry.

articleTitle: Design and Use of Protection-Class Rogowski Coils for Medium-Voltage Switchgear
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The Rogowski coil, a technology over a century old, capable of current measurement, has existed alongside current transformers since its inception but has never found significant use with a protective relay in medium-voltage switchgear. The application of the technology has been held back by its inability to drive electromechanical relays and a lack of standardization.However, the accepted solution (current transformers) has many issues and limitations, including the loss of measurement due to saturation, damage to the current transformer and switchgear from an open secondary, dynamic range limitations, and hazardous potential on the secondary terminals. These hazards, limitations, and vulnerabilities were accepted for a century with procedural or additive protections, leading to elevated risk. Technologies have now advanced to enable the use of Rogowski coils in lieu of the current transformer, supported by the guidance of international and domestic standards of protective relays.In this paper, we discuss the process of developing a Rogowski coil for the use and application in medium-voltage switchgear in combination with a protective relay.We further validate the performance of a relay that has Rogowski coil inputs against a calibrated reference sensor. We also show field results when the sensor is applied to a specialty system, like an arc-furnace.

articleTitle: Investigation of Lightning and Grounding Installation Practices That Resulted In A Turbine-Generator Failure Within An LNG Supplied Generation Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper presents a root cause analysis (RCA) of a lightning atmospheric event that caused the trip of a combined cycle power plant. It will concentrate on why the 138kV breaker for a 135 MVA steam generator (STG) opened under load during a lightning event. When the generator breaker opened, the steam turbine went into an overspeed condition. This resulted in the ejection of a 36-ton generator rotor. In contrast, the adjacent Gas Turbine Generator (GTG) continued to operate without incident. The GTG had proper electronic grounding, including connection to the ground grid and complete magnetic shielding of the entire control system. The RCA covered why the STG governor, Automatic Voltage Regulator (AVR) and control systems failed. It also addressed the installation and grounding design errors, antenna effects of grounding conductors, and electronic grounding of the generator controls. Other areas such as inadequate lightning protection, personnel step and touch potential safety design, transferred earth potentials, and the related LNG Gas supply were included. The reasons why the STG had an overspeed event will not be discussed in this paper since it was not part of the scope of the site RCA. Specific recommendations to prevent a re-occurrence will be presented and to improve the overall site performance unique to a coral-based rock location. Recommended improvements are in process.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Time Series Forecasting for Motor Winding Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Predictive maintenance of electric motors in large refineries is a challenge. Electric motors supply the power to key process equipment such as pumps and compressors, and their failure can lead to large financial losses. As such, it is essential to predict future condition of these motors in advance. The failure of the electric motors has been linked to some key parameters such as weather-related factors (i.e., ambient temperature, precipitation level, etc.), a motor’s bearing and winding temperatures, as well as motor’s operating current, for which telemetry data can be collected on a minute level.This work studies and applies use of classic time series techniques such as statistical models as well as machine learning solutions, post intensive data engineering and exploratory data analytics. Several different algorithms were studied and deployed to address both data engineering and data science scope of the work in an automated fashion to be implemented in machine learning operationalization. Eventually, a hybrid model (combined statistics and machine learning) was developed, tested and deployed on several electric motors with versatile attributes, and the models showed very good precision on the hold-out test data, with a long predictive power.Selected models are used to generate long term (up to six months) forecast for the average daily highest winding temperature.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion BMS Concepts for Industrial UPS Applications and Questions we Should be Asking
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: For typical industrial UPS and switchgear control applications, oil and gas, refinery, petrochemical, and offshore platform operations are beginning to transition from vented lead acid (VLA), valve regulated lead acid (VRLA), and nickel cadmium (Ni-Cd) batteries to modern battery technologies. Recognize that modern battery technologies require battery management and control systems that were not mandatory for VLA, VRLA, or Ni-Cd technologies.Lithium-Ion (Li-Ion) papers and presentations tend to highlight and promote the “advantages”, while providing only an overview of the Battery Management System (BMS). To increase awareness and understanding, the paper focus is the BMS systems for the authors conceptual example Li-Ion battery system used with a typical 120V industrial UPS with backup power in range of 15kVA to 200kVA and stored energy greater than 20kWh.Increasing BMS understanding is a major learning shift by industrial users because there is an emphasis on electronic circuit boards, integrated circuits, control algorithms, and communications. This does not require users to be circuit board designers but does require an interest and knowledge of the integrated circuits and algorithms used by the BMS system circuitry.Hopefully, this paper will encourage modern battery technology suppliers to provide more detailed BMS presentations and papers to alleviate the mystery and concerns about the BMS control methods and details for oil and gas, refinery, petrochemical, chemical, and offshore platform operations.Initially, this paper included Operational and Risk considerations, such as, factory acceptance testing (FAT), shipping, storage, commissioning, operating, and maintenance. Because of paper length constraints and the focus on the BMS, Operational and Risk considerations are planned for the next paper.

articleTitle: Enabling EPC 4.0 Using Integrated Power and Process Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This document provides an overview of the enduring benefits of an innovative approach for integrating automation and electrical control systems in capital projects, riding on the proven reliability of evolving technology. Integrating automation and electrical control systems is vital for project optimization, system simplicity, and operational efficiency in electro-intensive industrial plants. The value of integrated systems through the plant’s life cycle is proven. However, the approach struggles to gain wider acceptance due to organizational issues, differing standards and technology, and ill-defined digital transformation strategies. Integrated power and process designs provide significant capital expenditure savings opportunities and positively impact an electro-intensive plant’s operational performance and reliability. This paper discusses the challenges and advantages of power and process control integration and solutions strategies to help engineering, procurement, and construction companies as well as end-users.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Partial Discharge Database to Determine When Stator Winding Insulation Maintenance is Needed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: On-line partial discharge testing and monitoring have been widely applied by petrochemical industries on large motors and generators to determine the need for maintenance of the stator winding insulation system. Over the past 20 years, a single consistent method has been used to collect on-line PD data from over 22 000 motors and generators equipped with the required sensors. Of these, PD data from 8500 machines collected to the end of 2021 have been assembled into a single database, along with machine ratings and machine operating data. For each machine, the PD magnitude for each phase from the most recent test when the motor or generator was operating at normal load and stator winding operating temperature was statistically analyzed. The cumulative probability of occurrence for any PD activity level for any particular machine rating, manufacturing method and winding design etc. could then be produced. It has become clear that the probability distributions for different stator winding operating voltages produce statistically significant distributions for machines of various voltage ratings. Over the years, these probability tables have been correlated with visual inspections of hundreds of stator windings as well as off-line test results. This analysis indicates that when the PD magnitude is higher than about 90% of similar machines tested with the same method, then there is a very high probability of significant stator winding aging. This, combined with the evolution of PD over time, can be used to determine when maintenance is advisable.

articleTitle: Voltage Sensing and Measurement using OHMIC Voltage Sensors: An Improved Approach to Applications Traditionally Requiring 2.4 to 38 KV Voltage Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Voltage transformers and control power transformers traditionally have been core and coil designs. Because of the core and coil design (saturable inductance), when a traditional voltage transformer or control power transformer is switched or switching occurs in the primary circuit in which the transformer is connected, oscillatory switching transients are produced by the interaction of the switching device, transformer, load, and system, which may damage the internal insulation and fail the transformer. Having investigated several hundred medium voltage transformers and control power transformer failures and applied successful solutions, an alternate solution has become a necessity to mitigate against the primary switching transients and resonance problems associated with voltage transformers. Drawing on this experience gained, this paper introduces a modern approach for 2.4 to 38 kV voltage transformer applications utilizing voltage sensors consisting of Ohmic Voltage Sensors. The paper presents the ohmic voltage sensors technology as an alternate for conventional VTs and the often-needed transient mitigation. The paper describes the advantages of ohmic voltage sensors over conventional voltage transformers, the applicable standards, testing of the OVSs to prove accuracy for relaying and metering and application considerations. A case study for a major US chemical facility will illustrate the application of ohmic voltage sensors in lieu of traditional voltage transformers to mitigate against potential ferroresonance and switching transients’ events due to the operation of upstream breakers with the added benefit of reduced space constraints in the switchgear.

articleTitle: Improving the Bottom Line: How Gas-Insulated Substations can Offer Operational & Maintenance Cost Savings for Petrochemical Facilities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: To avoid production downtime, petrochemical facilities need reliable infrastructure. Gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) can often offer counterintuitive cost-effective solutions for petrochemical facilities that are considering new substation construction or upgrades to existing substations. Obstacles such as higher initial capital investment, lack of GIS operation and maintenance expertise, and sulfur hexafluoride gas (SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>) emissions concerns can prevent facilities from pursuing this option despite potential long-term savings. This paper offers solutions to these common roadblocks and presents several benefits that positively impact a facility’s bottom line. The paper explores long-term maintenance costs for GIS substations versus air-insulated substations; the lower costs of depreciation over a GIS substation’s longer useful life; and the greater reliability of GIS substations. Additional considerations that can impact operational and maintenance costs include reduced safety risks for personnel and enhanced equipment protection in high contamination environments. Installing modular GIS assemblies can also reduce construction time, minimizing potential disruptions to plant operations. Additionally, the historically predominant SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gas insulating medium, whose use is rapidly becoming more heavily regulated due to its environmental impact, is no longer the only option for GIS builds. New alternative insulation gas mixtures can eliminate the use of SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gas, helping facilities meet environmental sustainability goals.

articleTitle: Evolving Design and Worker Safety Standards for DC Power
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Technologies are rapidly evolving for the generation, transmission, and storage of DC power, requiring new or revised design and worker safety standards. Examples of these rapidly evolving technologies include solar and wind power generation, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and de transmission lines. This paper will provide an overview of evolving design standards (UL, IEC, and IEEE) for solar power generation, batteries, and battery energy storage systems, and the recent and upcoming revisions for worker safety standards and safe work practices covering the hazards of de, capacitors, and RF electrical hazards (NFPA and IEEE). Details of evolving de shock and arc flash hazards will be provided, included new models for the modeling of dynamic arc behavior.

articleTitle: Critical Infrastructure Protection With Modern Protection Relays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Hardening the electric-power grid has become important today because of threats to the electric infrastructure. These threats are not only from bad actors targeting operational security; threats come from protective-relay design problems and aging hardware. Modern microprocessor relays employ significant cyber defense and firmware advancements, as well as in physical improvements that increase reliability. These advancements include improved cybersecurity, power-supply longevity improvements, electromotive pulse (EMP)/geomagnetic disturbance (GMD) withstand, and advanced memory-map/bit-integrity safeguards. Misoperations data show greatly reduced incidents with new technology. New-generation relay designs include ease of upgrade from older relays via plug-n’-play retrofit solutions. Furthermore, software advances make settings and communications configurations easier, with fewer errors, which increase reliability of the electrical infrastructure. This paper reviews the latest advancements in relay design, construction, and software. In addition are recommendations for managing an aging relay fleet.

articleTitle: To Use an ASD or Not to Use an ASD: are You Saving or Wasting Money?
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: This paper presents an in-depth analysis of the efficiency profiles of different types of driven equipment with respect to their load and speed profiles, focusing on the use of adjustable speed drives (ASDs) to achieve energy cost reductions in industrial plants. Systematic methods for estimating the performance of an existing plant with relatively few known historic plant parameters are demonstrated, enabling plant owners to evaluate the opportunity or risk of installing an ASD. The study shows that utilizing ASDs to drive motors and driven equipment at reduced speeds, resulting in reduced production output, can lead to significant energy cost savings when applied to specific load types. However, if full-speed motor and load system production output is required for the operation of the plant output, the use of ASDs may be uneconomical. Furthermore, for material processing plants, the use of an ASD may directly reduce the plant’s production output. The study suggests that taking advantage of the torque multiplication advantage of a gearbox may provide significant advantages in capital procurement cost savings, standardization, plant design, and sizing in low-speed applications. Finally, the study warns against applying a sales brochure approach of “installing an ASD will save you energy” to the entire plant without performing energy and performance analysis. Overall, the findings of this study provide valuable insights for industrial plant owners to make informed decisions about the installation of ASDs to achieve energy cost savings while minimizing production losses.

articleTitle: Fire and Blast Hazards in Petrochemical Facilities: Design Practices for Electrical Enclosures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: In industrial processing facilities, power distribution equipment is typically housed in dedicated prefabricated enclosures, which are strategically laid out in the plant to distribute power to processing units. These enclosures can contain low voltage or medium voltage switchgear, motor control centers, battery systems for backup DC power, and other control and monitoring equipment. Although these enclosures are not typically occupied by personnel during plant operations, they play a key function in controlling processes, even in critical or emergency situations. Due to their critical function in controlling processes inside the plant, this paper recommends these enclosures be risk assessed to determine if they should be designed to reduce the impact that accidental fires or explosions could have on the enclosed equipment. This paper discusses existing industry practices and technical literature that covers the blast and fire design of electrical enclosures. It further discusses a real vapor cloud explosion accident (Texas City, 2005) [10] that caused unintentional blast loading on a power distribution building.

articleTitle: 1584.1 -2022 IEEE Guide for Scope and Deliverables Foran ARC-Flash Hazard Calculation Study what is it and Why do I Need It?
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: IEEE 1584.1™ - 2022 IEEE Guide for the Specification of Scope and Deliverable Requirements for an Arc-Flash Hazard Calculation Study in Accordance with IEEE Std 1584™ was published in 2022 [1], This paper provides an overview of the standard to the users and practitioners who requisition or conduct arc-flash studies and emphasizes the proper use of checklists to define scope and deliverables. The purpose of this standard is to enable stakeholders to understand the minimum scope of work and deliverables required for an arc-flash study. Stakeholders include, but are not limited to employers, owners, operators, and contractors as well as those who are responsible for the specification or the performance of a study. Checklists are provided with detailed task matrices to help define the scope of work and responsibilities for gathering data and deliverables for arc-flash hazard calculation studies. The terminology used in this standard is based on equipment and practices in North America. This paper provides information on how this standard can be used internationally to define scope and deliverables of an arc-flash hazard calculation study.

articleTitle: Three Plane Motor Balancing: Do i Need it or Not
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Rotor balancing is an essential part of ensuring proper motor operation. While typical specifications (API 541, API 684, MIL-STD-167-1A) require a multi-plane balance for rotors which go through the first bending critical, the details of how the balance should be performed and to what limits, is sparse. This paper will establish the best practices for when multi-plane balancing is beneficial, what the procedure should look like, as well as how to determine acceptance criteria for such a rotor. Additionally, it will be presented that a rotor could be designed such that it requires only 2-plane balancing even when operating above the first bending critical.A case study that explores the downside of not implementing multi-plane balancing techniques will be examined. Specifically, it will demonstrate how improving the balance of a flexible shaft rotor at operating speed caused the vibration to intensify at the critical speed.The described best practices combined with a fundamental understanding of the requirements for rotor balancing and proper applications will help manufacturers, system packagers and end users to be confident that their rotating machine has a quality balance throughout the entire speed range (including variable frequency drive operation) and will provide years of service.

articleTitle: Expected Sources of Energies in Hazardous Spectrum and Their Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: At the 2018 IEEE PCIC a paper was presented titled “Unexpected Sources of Energies Weeding through Hazardous Spectrum” [1], In addition to sparking and hot surfaces, that paper addressed restricted use of electronic devices such as cell phones or tablets in classified hazardous locations or “Explosive Atmospheres”. Since then, advancement in technology and changes in the certification standards has made the landscape of mobility devices including smart phones, and tablets a bit more confusing when it comes to its use in classified hazardous locations, such as Class I, Division 1 and 2, and Zone 1 and 2. This paper will cover in detail the design aspects of these pieces of equipment as well as their development and deployment in the field to ensure safe working conditions. Additionally, it will cover some updates in the standards to clarify what is appropriate and what is not, when verifying if equipment is safe for use in classified hazardous locations. While it can be challenging to do, equipment can be properly designed and certified for use in a classified hazardous location, for global use. Applicable standards are in place and continuous technology improvement renders these certified devices accessible and available to the market for use in hazardous locations. These certified devices serve the needs of several end users across the globe for certified safety in these devices allowing them to benefit from advanced technology in hazardous locations.

articleTitle: Stator Winding Insulation System Per Iec 60079-7, What, Why, How, Pros and Cons.
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Standard IEC 60079-7 [1] describes Type of Protection increased safety “e”. For Level of Protection “eb” machines for use in Zone 1 or Class I, Division 1 hazardous locations, if the rated voltage exceeds 1 kV, a stator winding insulation type test is required. For Level of Protection “ec” machines for use in Zone 2 or Division 2 hazardous locations, the requirement for type tests differs based on the equipment group, rated voltage, and the type of the winding. This paper will discuss in depth the winding insulation system for the synchronous and asynchronous motors including insulation system materials and process differences needed to meet the test requirements. The paper will cover the test procedures, requirement for test samples, details for performing the test and evaluating the test results. It discusses further advantages and disadvantages of the test, passing the tests, and the long-term reliability of the winding insulation system. The impact of failures occurring in service with respect to rebuild/rewinding if required, ensuring or validating duplicate winding by a repair shop if not rebuilt at the OEM. The paper has input from OEMs, testing facilities, certifiers, and end users.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Using a VSD in a Mining Installation, Analysis, and Measured Results
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Energy Efficiency has been in the spotlight of electrical engineering, driving research for technological advances and modernization of installed industrial applications. Electrical equipment suppliers and manufacturers have often acted as promotors of using Variable Speed Drives with Energy Savings to lower the end user’s energy bill and quickly obtain a return on investment. Many offline and online tools serve as means to estimate energy savings when changing a Direct-on-Line motor-driven application to use Variable Speed Drives to reduce energy consumption by correctly adjusting speed and Torque to what the load indeed requires, instead of using throttling in the case of pumps or dampers in the case of fans. However, it is rare to find a complete compilation from the initial study case to installation and operation, estimating energy savings compared to the actual measured outcome. Therefore, this paper presents a comprehensive assessment, analysis, recommendation, implementation, and onsite results.

articleTitle: Energy Prescription For The Petrochemical Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The Petro-Chemical Industry is under attack for its production of fossil fuels and the concerns over CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(CO2) emissions. While there is no debate concerning the increase of CO2 levels into the atmosphere from the use of fossil fuels, there is an issue about the impact of increased CO. This paper shows the need for fossil fuels into the foreseeable future to not only supply existing needs but increased loads that are going to be driven by industry. The use of fossil fuels will be compared to that of modern-day medicines with similar logic on the needs, uses and side effects. A solution to the energy and emissions concerns of hydrocarbons will be shown to not only exist, but the solution is basic and economical in nature.

articleTitle: The Use of Advanced Catalytic Technology in a Methane Abatement Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas and one of the main contributors to climate change. The reduction of methane in our atmosphere to reduce global warming and its effect on climate change has become a global concern. In support of achieving this goal is the need to develop implementable methane abatement solutions. This paper presents such a solution using advanced catalytic technologies and recommends new applications that can provide significant reduction in the emission of methane.

articleTitle: Electrical Design in Petrochemical Facilities - Considerations for Reducing the Environmental Impact
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE IAS Petroleum and Chemical Industry Technical Conference (PCIC)
abstract: The last several years have seen an increased focus on evaluating the environmental impact of projects from inception to end of life. Support from stakeholders, technologies from equipment manufacturers, and developments in codes and standards have made it realistic to improve the delivery of traditional petrochemical projects. This paper surveys methods of saving energy, reducing waste material, minimizing transportation, and minimizing emissions and discharges through the entire lifecycle of a project. This includes choices in power generation (both permanent and temporary), choosing lower consumption or carbon footprint equipment, construction techniques, and digital tools. Voluntary and mandatory requirements are discussed in relation to the North American environment. The intent is to show that, given the initiative and mindset, substantial improvements can be attained for all projects.
